preRegisteredFalsifiers.dispatchText: A county with no writer run and no verdict change since its last publish is skipped, with the reason.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.preRegisteredAnswer: SKIP with reason UNCHANGED_SINCE_LAST_PRODUCTION_PUBLISH, carrying: the last production publish (publish_runs.id + completed_at + the publish run's started_at), the counts of writer run records/runs examined, and the verdict comparison (baseline observed-at + changed-rail count = 0). Nothing is published, no child execution is dispatched.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.provedBy: test/republish-on-change.test.mjs, test named 'F1 ...', against a fake factory client whose county has a publish and no writer evidence; asserts the summary's disposition and that the publish executor was never called.

preRegisteredFalsifiers.dispatchText: A county whose writer ran after its last publish is selected, with the run id as evidence.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.preRegisteredAnswer: SELECT with reason WRITER_RUN_AFTER_PUBLISH (or WRITER_STAGE_RECORD_AFTER_PUBLISH), evidence naming the run_id(s) and their ended_at/started_at, compared against the publish run's started_at.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.provedBy: test/republish-on-change.test.mjs, test named 'F2 ...'; the summary's `evidence` array must contain the literal run id from the fixture, and the county must appear in `selected`.

preRegisteredFalsifiers.dispatchText: Without --apply, nothing is published (test with a fake publish).
preRegisteredFalsifiers.preRegisteredAnswer: With no --apply, the job resolves the same selection, dispatches NO child execution (the fake publish records zero calls), writes a dry-run P-284 stage record per county (run_mode='dry-run', run_id NULL) and exits 0.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.provedBy: test/republish-on-change.test.mjs, test named 'F3 ...'; asserts publishCalls === 0 while a selected county exists, and that every county in scope got a stage record with run_mode 'dry-run'.

preRegisteredFalsifiers.dispatchText: A publish that requirePreBakeReadiness refuses stops the job for that county and is recorded.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.preRegisteredAnswer: The child publish exits non-zero; the job reads back the child run's refuse_code (the gate's own code, written by bastrop-publish.mjs's catch as runs.refuse_code) and records the county as REFUSED_<CODE> with the code and the child execution name on the stage record (outcome 'refused', instrument_verdict 'publish-refused:<code>'). No further child execution is dispatched for that county (production is not attempted after a refused staging publish). Other counties in the same loop are unaffected.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.provedBy: test/republish-on-change.test.mjs, test named 'F4 ...'; a fake executor that fails the staging child plus a fake reads of runs.refuse_code = 'RAIL_UNACCOUNTED' must produce disposition refused with that code in the summary and on the stage record, and the executor must see exactly one call for that county.

preRegisteredFalsifiers.preRegisteredAnswer: The signal must be able to say CHANGED and must be able to say UNCHANGED; a fixture where the writer run is one second BEFORE the publish start must read unchanged, and the same fixture moved one second after must read changed. A signal that only ever answers one way is not an instrument.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.provedBy: test/republish-on-change.test.mjs, test named 'the boundary is the publish run's start, and it is exercised on both sides'.

changeSignal.missionText: decide whether the ledger changed since the county's last successful production publish; do not compute max(updated_at) over a county's cells
changeSignal.measuredAgainst: the factory store (Neon project withered-surf-26870298 'hauska-factory', branch main br-noisy-bar-au9cwf7n), read-only role parcel_record_ro, 2026-09-17T00:42-00:58Z

tablesAndQueries.name: Q1 the published boundary (publish run records)
tablesAndQueries.sql: SELECT id, county_fips, target, status, completed_at, created_at FROM publish_runs WHERE county_fips = $1 AND target = 'production' AND status = 'succeeded' ORDER BY completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, created_at DESC LIMIT 1
tablesAndQueries.index: publish_runs_county_target (county_fips, target, created_at DESC) -- read live from pg_indexes 2026-09-17
tablesAndQueries.secondHalf: the publish's START is not on publish_runs: bastrop-publish.mjs inserts the row with completed_at = now() AFTER the bakes, so the boundary is read from runs.started_at for the same id (publish_runs.id === runs.id for every publish, randomUUID minted once in runBastropPublish and passed to both startRun and the publish_runs INSERT)
tablesAndQueries.sql2: SELECT started_at, phase, status FROM runs WHERE id = $1
tablesAndQueries.index2: runs_pkey (id) -- and this is the ONLY index on runs (read live 2026-09-17), so every other runs predicate in this design is a sequential scan of 3,643 rows / 2.4 MB (reltuples, stored statistic)
tablesAndQueries.plan: index scan by (county_fips, target, created_at DESC) then LIMIT 1; NOT observed as EXPLAIN -- see measurementBoundary

tablesAndQueries.name: Q2 the county-keyed writer stage records (P-284 grain)
tablesAndQueries.sql: SELECT s.id, s.run_id, s.stage, s.stage_detail, s.started_at, s.ended_at, s.outcome, s.rows_written, s.rows_written_basis, r.phase, r.status, r.refuse_code FROM stage_run_records s LEFT JOIN runs r ON r.id = s.run_id WHERE s.county_fips = $1 AND s.stage = ANY($2::smallint[]) AND s.started_at > $3 ORDER BY s.started_at DESC LIMIT 20
tablesAndQueries.plan: bitmap/index scan on (county_fips, stage) with the ANY list, filter on started_at, then sort. Bounded by the county's own rows in 5 of 13 stages. NOT observed as EXPLAIN -- see measurementBoundary
tablesAndQueries.liveState: stage_run_records carries 4 rows in total (reltuples, live 2026-09-17). The county-keyed writer record this signal wants therefore barely exists today: the rail writers do not write stage records yet (stage-map.mjs own ownerRow for them is P-285). This is why the runs half below is not optional.

tablesAndQueries.name: Q3 writer RUN records, county-matched (the half that exists today)
tablesAndQueries.sql: SELECT r.id, r.phase, r.status, r.started_at, r.target, r.scope, r.counts FROM runs r WHERE r.started_at > $1 AND r.phase = ANY($2::text[]) AND (r.scope->>'county' = $3 OR r.scope->>'countyFips' = $3 OR (jsonb_typeof(r.scope->'counties') = 'array' AND r.scope->'counties' ? $3)) ORDER BY r.started_at DESC LIMIT 20
tablesAndQueries.index: none usable: runs has runs_pkey only (live 2026-09-17). The plan is a sequential scan of 3,643 rows / 2.4 MB, measured as a stored statistic, not a count.
tablesAndQueries.whyItIsStillCheap: the 76M-row / 26 GB table the dispatch forbids scanning is parcel_record_cell (reltuples 76,055,440 / 26 GB, live). runs is 2.4 MB -- three orders of magnitude smaller. The query is bounded on started_at first and the phase list is short.
tablesAndQueries.knownUnderCoverage: writer jobs frequently do NOT name a county in runs.scope: measured in source, parcel-r5-zoning.mjs:950-957 sets scope = { job, cities, excludedStampGap, apply, method_version, nowIso } -- no county key. A county-keyed match therefore MISSES those runs. The stage-record half (Q2) is the county-keyed record and is the reason P-284 exists at all; until P-285 wires the rail writers, a run that names no county is invisible to this signal and that is declared, not hidden.
tablesAndQueries.phaseSet: the writer phases are DERIVED, not hardcoded: every phase in PHASE_STAGE whose stage is 3, 4, 5, 6 or 7 (acquire, identity, instantiate, rail fill, atoms) via stageForPhase() from src/lib/stage-map.mjs. A new writer phase added to the stage map is covered by the signal the day it is mapped.

tablesAndQueries.name: Q4 the gate verdicts (the only existing record whose value is a function of the cells)
tablesAndQueries.sql: SELECT rail_key, verdict, unaccounted_count, evaluated_at, run_id FROM parcel_gate_verdict WHERE county_fips = $1 ORDER BY rail_key
tablesAndQueries.plan: OBSERVED, live: 'Sort -> Seq Scan on parcel_gate_verdict (Filter: county_fips = 48453)', cost 16.84..17.01, 65 rows -- the planner prefers a seq scan because the whole table is 391 rows / 184 kB (reltuples + pg_total_relation_size, live). This is the one plan in this CP1 that is literal EXPLAIN output.
tablesAndQueries.theHeartbeatFinding: evaluated_at CANNOT be the signal. UPSERT_VERDICT_SQL (src/jobs/publish-gate-sched.mjs:325-330) has no WHERE on its DO UPDATE, so every scheduler run rewrites evaluated_at for every rail; measured live 2026-09-17T00:42Z: county 48021's 65 rails carry evaluated_at spread over 22:41:42..22:43:29 from ONE run_id, and the newest verdict anywhere is within minutes of the query. A predicate of the form `evaluated_at > lastPublish` therefore reads 'changed' for every county on every cycle -- a false-positive machine, not a signal. The signal is the VERDICT VALUE compared against a recorded baseline; the evaluated_at half of the dispatch's phrasing is refuted by measurement and by source, and that refutation is the deliverable here.

tablesAndQueries.name: Q5 the verdict baseline (the gap this lane had to solve without new schema)
tablesAndQueries.problem: parcel_gate_verdict holds only the CURRENT verdict per (county, rail) -- there is no history table, no verdict-change column, and the publish's own pre-bake-readiness run_event records COUNTS ONLY (bastrop-publish.mjs:288-303 writes counts/bakeVsRoll/.../railsChecked, never the per-rail verdict map). So 'a verdict changed' is not answerable from existing rows without a stored baseline.
tablesAndQueries.solution: the job records its own observation of each county's verdict map (per-rail verdict + a sha256 digest of the sorted rail=verdict lines + observedAt) in ITS OWN runs row, `counts->'gateVerdictBaseline'`, and reads the previous observation back from the most recent prior run of its own phase: SELECT id, started_at, counts FROM runs WHERE phase = 'republish-on-change' AND id <> $1 ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1. No new table, no new column, no migration.
tablesAndQueries.whyNotRunEvents: run_events is 41,544 rows / 105 MB and has NO index on run_id (only run_events_pkey on id, live) -- reading a snapshot back from it is a 105 MB sequential scan per cycle. This was checked and rejected on measurement, not on preference.
tablesAndQueries.whyNotCellsUpdatedAt: REFUSED BY THE DISPATCH and confirmed by plan: see theForbiddenScan below.
tablesAndQueries.firstCycleBehaviour: with no prior observation the gate dimension is UNMEASURED with reason NO_BASELINE_OBSERVATION and does NOT by itself select the county. Declared, not silently read as 'unchanged'.
tablesAndQueries.declaredBlindSpot: a verdict that changes and reverts between two cycles is invisible to this comparison (an instrument's exclusion set is part of its contract, DEV_PROCESS 2.x).

theForbiddenScan.dispatchText: Do not compute max(updated_at) over a county's cells (a heavy scan on a 76M-row table).
theForbiddenScan.confirmedHow: EXPLAIN only, nothing executed, live 2026-09-17. parcel_record_cell has NO county_fips column at all (columns read live: place_key, rail_key, cell_state, updated_at), so a county scope is only expressible as a place_key prefix, and no index on updated_at exists (indexes read live: PK (place_key, rail_key), (rail_key), partial (place_key) WHERE kind='unaccounted').
literalPlans: max(updated_at) WHERE place_key LIKE '48453:%'  ->  Finalize Aggregate / Gather / Parallel Seq Scan on parcel_record_cell, Filter: place_key ~~ '48453:%', cost=2794686.95..2794686.96, rows 12,476,261 of ~31.7M scanned
max(updated_at) WHERE place_key >= '48453:' AND place_key < '48454:'  ->  Parallel Seq Scan, cost=2872813.02..2872813.03
GROUP BY left(place_key,5) over all counties  ->  Parallel Seq Scan, cost=2925547.31..2937849.72
theForbiddenScan.corroboration: src/lib/parcel-record-engine/load.js:88-90 already records the same shape timing out: the place_key-range form 'timed out at 120s against Travis (48453, 380,917 ...)'. Two independent measurements, one query plan and one execution history, agree with the dispatch's premise.
theForbiddenScan.tableSize: parcel_record_cell: reltuples 76,055,440, 26 GB total (live). parcel_record: 981,267 rows / 160 MB, indexed on county_fips. Bastrop's record count measured live: 24,988.

decision.boundary: the publish RUN's started_at (the moment the bake began reading the ledger), not completed_at (written after the bakes). A writer whose work STARTED after that moment is not provably inside the bake, so it counts as a change; this is the conservative side and it converges because the boundary moves forward after every publish.
decision.changedIf: (a) a writer-stage stage_run_record for the county started after the boundary; OR (b) a writer-phase runs row naming the county started after the boundary; OR (c) the county's stored verdict map differs from the job's own last recorded observation of it; OR (d) the county has NO succeeded production publish at all.
decision.unchangedIf: a succeeded production publish exists, and (a), (b), (c) are all empty and (d) false.
decision.neverSilent: the summary and the stage record carry, per county, the boundary's timestamp and source, the counts examined in each dimension, and every named absence (NO_BASELINE_OBSERVATION, NEVER_PUBLISHED_PRODUCTION, PHASE_UNASSIGNED phases the signal cannot see).
decision.declaredFalsePositive: dollar-fields-patch is mapped to stage 6 by stage-map.mjs and writes the SERVE store (place_layer_snapshots), not the ledger, so a run of it can select a county whose ledger did not change. It is INCLUDED rather than excluded (the cost of a false positive is one publish; the cost of a false negative is stale served data) and named here.

flags: --apply (required to publish anything; absent = dry run)
--county=<fips> (repeatable; default = the six onboarded counties from texasCtxProgramConfig().programCountyFips)
--target=staging|production (default both, staging first, per the publish's own Rule 6)
--signal-only (report the signal and exit; no child)
sequencePerCounty: report changed/unchanged with evidence (dry run stops here and writes its stage record)
changed + --apply: dispatch factory-bastrop-publish --target=staging --county=<fips> --skip-pmtiles, waiting for the execution
read the child's own runs row back (scope->>'execution' = the execution name the Cloud Run API returned, or the newest publish_runs row for that county+target) for status and refuse_code
only on a staging success: dispatch --target=production with the execution-time env override OPERATOR_PUBLISH_GO=1 (and PRODUCTION_SITE_URL when the job has it), waiting for the execution
record the county's stage record (outcome, rows written from the publish's own tier1Summary, the trigger evidence, the cost) and the served bakedAt hook
jobDesign.oneAtATime: the loop is strictly sequential, stalest-first (ordered by the last production publish ascending, never-published first), capped by --max-counties, exactly as the dispatch requires.
jobDesign.dryRunDefault: runBastropPublish itself refuses --dry-run (DRY_RUN_REFUSED) and refuses a production publish without OPERATOR_PUBLISH_GO (OPERATOR_GO_REQUIRED); this job never passes --dry-run to the child and never injects OPERATOR_PUBLISH_GO for a staging publish or without --apply. Two independent refusals, not one.
jobDesign.refusalPropagation: the child's refuse_code is read back from runs.refuse_code (bastrop-publish.mjs:652) and recorded; a refused staging publish ends the county's sequence (production is never attempted after it) and the county is recorded 'refused' -- falsifier 4.
jobDesign.stageRecords: one stage_run_records row per (county, run) at stage 10 ('publish and serve'), via src/control/stage-runs.mjs openStageRun/closeStageRun. EVERY county handed to the loop gets a row, including an unchanged one (outcome succeeded, rows_written 0 with its basis) -- the P-284 audit reads run.scope.counties and demands a record for each, so skipping a county would fail that audit. run_mode='apply' with the run id when --apply, run_mode='dry-run' with run_id NULL otherwise (stage-runs.mjs refuses a dry run that names a run).
jobDesign.stageMapEntry: a NEW phase key 'republish-on-change' -> {stage: 10, stage_detail: '', writesRecords: true, writtenBy: ['republish-on-change.mjs']} in src/lib/stage-map.mjs, with its evidence. It cannot reuse the existing 'publish' entry: that entry is writesRecords:false and stage-map.test.mjs proves the false claim by asserting that the file it names does NOT import ../control/stage-runs.mjs -- bastrop-publish.mjs does not and must not be edited by this lane. The non-vacuity pin in test/p284-stage-run-records.test.mjs ('exactly 2 phases write records') becomes 3 and is updated with that fact stated.

leaseInteraction.dispatchText: takes P-281's lease (the publish already takes a job-execution lease on the target store; state how the two interact)
leaseInteraction.thisJob: one lease for the whole loop, on the FACTORY store's own host fingerprint: grantHeavyScanLease(factoryClient, {windowKind: 'job-execution', phase: 'republish-on-change', holder: leaseHolder(env), countyFips: null, runId, ttlMs}), released in a finally, with the release outcome naming the loop's outcome. A second concurrent republish-on-change run is refused LEASE_HELD and the refusal is written to heavy_scan_lease_refusals by the same module.
leaseInteraction.thePublish: each child publish takes its OWN job-execution lease, on the TARGET store's host (storeRefFromUrl(stores.HAUSKA_MCP_DATABASE_URL), alias '<var>:<target>'), phase 'publish', naming its own run id (bastrop-publish.mjs runChunkedConformantBakes:385-425).
leaseInteraction.howTheyInteract: they are two DIFFERENT databases, so they never contend with each other: the contention key is the host (0013_heavy_scan_leases.sql:26-31), the factory store is Neon project withered-surf-26870298 and the publish targets are cortex-prod (fancy-fire-06136146) -- the CTX-F note in cloudbuild.publish.yaml:380-385 states that NEONDB and HAUSKA_MCP are the same Neon project, and it is not the factory's. The loop lease therefore protects 'one republish loop at a time' and cannot deadlock against the publish's own lease. What DOES contend is a cell writer holding a heavy-scan lease on the target store: the child publish's lease take then refuses LEASE_HELD, the child exits non-zero, and this job records that refusal for the county and moves on -- the second lease is enforced inside the child, not re-implemented here.
leaseInteraction.targetStoreSeqScan: not applicable to this job: it reads no cell tables at all (see theForbiddenScan). The heavy read is inside the child publish, which takes its lease before its first bake.

scheduleProposal.definition: scripts/schedulers/republish-on-change.scheduler.json (checked in, NOT created and NOT enabled -- a definition for the integration seat to create)
scheduleProposal.whyItFits: the loop is bounded by two numbers the repo already fixes: the per-county publish task-timeout is 6h (cloudbuild.publish.yaml factory-bastrop-publish TIMEOUT=21600) and the per-run county cap is --max-counties (default 2). Worst case per cycle is therefore 2 x 6h = 12h before the served-bakedAt hook and stage records are written, which fits inside a 6h cadence only for the COMMON case (0 or 1 changed county) and not the capped worst case. The honest proposal the integration seat should enable is therefore: --max-counties=1 with a 6h cadence (worst case 6h == the cadence, uncomfortable), or --max-counties=2 with a 12h cadence. This lane proposes 6h with --max-counties=1 as the DEFAULT (one county at a time, oldest-served first, which is also law 3's 'one county at a time until the farm is proven') and states the 12h/2 alternative rather than picking quietly.
scheduleProposal.overlapSafety: a cycle that overlaps the previous one is refused LEASE_HELD by the loop lease and recorded, never queued or interleaved.

hook.dispatchText: Record, per county, the served bakedAt the publish produces, so the integration seat can grade 'served bakedAt is later than the latest cell write, within one cycle'.
hook.servedSource: the value the CUSTOMER surface reads, traced to source and not assumed: LDT artifacts/api-server/src/routes/propertyExplorer.ts:625-637 returns bakedAt from loadBakedNodeFacetSnapshot, which (brokerageNodeFacets.ts:179-207) selects payload_json + snapshot_at from place_layer_snapshots WHERE adapter_key = 'node-facets:tier1' AND place_key = 'node:<countyFips>:<propId>'. The doc_repo's own customer instrument reads the same field (scripts/surface-probe.mjs:215 bakedAt).

whatIsRecordedPerCounty.servedBakedAt: SELECT payload_json->>'bakedAt' AS baked_at, snapshot_at FROM place_layer_snapshots WHERE adapter_key = 'node-facets:tier1' AND place_key = $1 LIMIT 1 -- for ONE named parcel per county, selected by the DECLARED rule 'the county's walk gold parcel (verify-walk.mjs resolveGold), i.e. the parcel the publish's own verifying walk grades'. A single-row lookup on the serve table's (place_key, adapter_key) index, not a county aggregate.
whatIsRecordedPerCounty.whyOneNamedParcel: a county-wide max(snapshot_at) over place_layer_snapshots is an unindexed aggregate over the county's snapshots; the named parcel is the parcel the publish already proved, so it is the reading with an owner. Stated as a SAMPLE with its selection rule (DEV_PROCESS 1.1: a sample travels with its rule), and its limit is named: verify-before-promote can legitimately decline to re-stamp a row whose new payload scores lower, so one parcel is not proof the whole county advanced.
whatIsRecordedPerCounty.factoryStamp: freshness.stamped_at + body.publishRunId for scope_key 'production:<county>' -- the factory's own record of the bake that is now served, read back after the publish (the publish upserts it at bastrop-publish.mjs:576-581).
whatIsRecordedPerCounty.latestCellWrite: the newest writer-stage stage_run_record's ended_at for the county (the 'latest cell write' the integration seat grades against), or the newest writer-phase run's started_at when no stage record exists.
whatIsRecordedPerCounty.gradeRule: served bakedAt > latestCellWrite, within one cycle -- recorded as a string with its two inputs, never as a bare boolean that hides which side was absent.

hook.whereWritten: one run_events row per county, kind 'served-baked-at', on THIS job's run (run_events has 41,544 rows / 105 MB and is written by the publish path already, so the grain is existing); plus instrument_verdict on the county's stage record and the full object in the job's stdout JSON.
hook.unmeasuredPath: when the serve store is not reachable or the named parcel has no tier1 row, the hook records an absence with a named reason (SERVE_STORE_UNREACHABLE / NO_TIER1_ROW_FOR_GOLD_PARCEL), never a zero or a copied factory stamp standing in for the served value.

measurementBoundary.readOnlyRole: the granted read-only role on the factory store is parcel_record_ro and its SELECT grant covers only parcel_gate_verdict, parcel_record, parcel_record_cell, parcel_record_companion_row (read live from information_schema.tables under that role, 2026-09-17).
measurementBoundary.consequence: literal EXPLAIN for Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5 (publish_runs, runs, stage_run_records, run_events, freshness) was REFUSED with 'permission denied for table <name>' under that role. Their plans above are therefore the index the planner must use, named from the live catalog (pg_indexes), and are labelled not-observed. The one observed plan in this CP1 is Q4's, plus the three forbidden-scan plans (parcel_record_cell IS in the grant).
measurementBoundary.notWorkedAround: the owner credential (neondb_owner) was NOT fetched to obtain those plans. Reading a production owner credential to improve a checkpoint's evidence is not this lane's call; the integration seat holds the job credential that will run these queries and can EXPLAIN them there.
measurementBoundary.noSecretPrinted: no connection string, password or role token appears in this artifact or in any command output this lane produced.

openFindings: the heartbeat: evaluated_at is rewritten for every rail on every scheduler run (source + live), so the dispatch's 'evaluated_at and verdict changed' can only be the verdict half; recorded above with both measurements.

stage_run_records is nearly empty live (4 rows), so the county-keyed writer signal is thin until P-285 wires the rail writers; runs is the half that works today and it under-covers county-unnamed writers (measured in parcel-r5-zoning.mjs).

the read-only grant on the factory store does not cover the six factory tables a lane would need to check this signal by hand; a lane can read the LEDGER cells with it but not the run records. Named for the seat that owns grants.
